<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

- The NPU precise-test pipeline always runs the full base-b/base-c suites when the
  coverage-based recommendation is empty. When a PR only touches product code under
  `python/sglang/` and the baseline recommends nothing, those suite runs burn NPU
  runner hours without producing signal. An empty recommendation is only trustworthy
  in that case: changes to tests, scripts, or workflows are invisible to the coverage
  baseline, so those PRs must keep the full-suite fallback.
- `recommend-tests-from-coverage` still ran (downloading the OBS baseline and building
  the test-case map) after `pr-gate` had already failed — wasted work for a doomed run.
- The published `outputs.tar.gz` (~300 MB) bundled the raw per-test coverage data that
  only manual map rebuilds need, while the recommend job consumes just the covstub
  source tree; the raw data was also unreachable without shared-disk access.
- `setup-covstub` occupied an aarch64 NPU-pool runner with a CANN image selected by
  `set-image-config`, although it only does CPU work (tar + python).
- `coveragerc` omitted `python/sglang/test/` and `python/sglang/benchmark/`, so those
  module trees never entered the baseline map or the coverage reports.

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

## Modifications

- **Skip-all rule for empty recommendations**
  - `test_selector.py`: extract every changed path from the PR diff into
    `pr_changed_files.txt` (PR mode only).
  - `bucket_recommended_tests.py`: new `--changed-files` input; when nothing was
    recommended and every changed path is under `python/sglang/`, emit
    `should_run_<suite>=false` for all suites and surface an "All suites skipped"
    note in the step summary. Existing safety fallbacks (empty suite enumeration,
    failed step -> empty outputs) still yield full-suite runs.
  - `pr-test-npu.yml`: pass `pr_changed_files.txt` to the bucketing step.
- **Gate the recommend job on the PR gate**: `recommend-tests-from-coverage` now has
  `needs: pr-gate` and `if: !failure() && !cancelled() && ...`, so it is skipped once
  the gate fails.
- **Move `setup-covstub` off the NPU pool**: `runs-on: linux-amd64-cpu-4` with the
  fixed `ascend-ci/sglang:main-x86` image; dropped the `set-image-config` dependency
  (and its CANN image output); `pip` -> `python3 -m pip`.
- **Slimmer, split baseline artifacts**
  - `outputs.tar.gz` now packages only `outputs/covstub` (a few MB instead of ~300 MB).
  - Raw per-test coverage data is archived separately as `coverage-data.tar.gz`,
    uploaded as the `precise-test-coverage-data` artifact (14-day retention) and
    published to the shared disk (guarded, absent when no data was collected) for
    manual map rebuilds.
  - `htmlcov`/`htmlcov-npu` artifacts get `retention-days: 14`; the base-a coverage
    relay artifact drops from 7 to 1 day.
- **coveragerc**: stop omitting `*/sglang/test/*` and `*/sglang/benchmark/*` so those
  module trees are recorded in the baseline map and reports.
- Comment compression across `pr-test-npu.yml` and `coverage-collection-npu.yml`
  (no behavior change).

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

-# Coverage data collection pipeline for the NPU precision test selection.
+# Coverage baseline collection for the NPU precision test selection.
 # Delegates to pr-test-npu.yml with coverage_mode=true, which switches:
-#   - Runners to the coverage pool (shared /root/.cache with setup-covstub)
-#   - use_coverage_runner=true on all test jobs
-#   - Runs the base-a unit suite on the coverage pool (base-a-test-npu-cov)
+#   - Test jobs to the coverage pool with use_coverage_runner=true
+#   - base-a to a hosted runner (base-a-test-npu-cov, data merged via artifact)
 #   - Runs the multimodal-gen suites too. Their runner is asked for this
 #     shard's targets (case-level pytest node ids) and each target is run in
 #     its own coverage invocation, so diffusion coverage is attributed per
 #     test case instead of per shard.
-#   - Skips pr-gate, recommend, analyze
-#   - Runs setup-covstub to assemble coverage data and publish it to the
-#     shared disk at a fixed path (/root/.cache/tests/precise-test/coverage)
-# pr-test-npu-finish is the final gate in the called workflow.
-#
-# Manually triggered only (workflow_dispatch): PRs run the standard
-# pr-test-npu.yml instead; this pipeline builds the full coverage baseline
-# on demand.
+#   - Skips pr-gate, recommend
+#   - setup-covstub assembles and publishes the baseline to the shared disk
+#     at /root/.cache/tests/precise-test/coverage
+# pr-test-npu-finish is the final gate in the called workflow. Manually
+# triggered only (workflow_dispatch): PRs run the standard pr-test-npu.yml
+# instead; this pipeline builds the full coverage baseline on demand.
 name: Coverage Collection (NPU)
